description_full: Friedman Industries, Incorporated engages in the manufacture and processing of steel products in the United States. The company operates in two segments, Flat-Roll Products and Tubular Products. The Flat-Roll Product segment is involved in the operation of hot-rolled coil processing facilities to cut the coils into sheets and plates, as well as the provision of process and storage services for customer-owned coils on a fee basis. The Tubular Product segment manufactures line and oil country pipes, as well as pipes for structural applications. The company serves metals distributors and customers manufacturing products, such as metal buildings, railcars, heavy equipment, tanks and containers, trailers, component parts, and other fabricated metal products. Friedman Industries, Incorporated was incorporated in 1965 and is headquartered in Longview, Texas.

financial_summary: Friedman Industries Inc. is a micro-cap basic materials business with a $260M market cap on $445M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +16% over the past three years and +18% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 17% against a 10% cost of capital, a 6-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it.
The company is burning through $8M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 40× is fortress-like.
Shareholder yield is only 0.5%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 6.5% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.1× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

val: The stock trades 69% below its DCF fair value of $116, a meaningful margin of safety.
